column1: # scripts/known-deviations.issues.tsv — the issues the known deviations name, with the rule each one
# does not meet and the observable difference (#1126 S2).
# Columns, TAB-separated: issue number, rule not met (spec chapter and section, or decision ID),
# observable difference, and `rows` when scripts/known-deviations.tsv names it or `none` when the
# deviation has no fixture row: no program-visible value differs (the defect is in how the result is
# reached), or the pinned revision's rule is not implemented yet and its issue carries the reproduction.
# Every issue here must be open: scripts/land.sh PHASE 2 refuses a closed one, and
# `scripts/fixture_expect.sh --issues-open` asks `gh` by hand. The gate holds the rest without network.

column3: `not a < b` parses as `not (a < b)`, so a numeric `not 255 < x` compiles and runs instead of being refused; `alatyr fmt` strips the parentheses of `not (a < b)`

column3: wat: `target.os` answers `linux` and `target.env` `gnu`, so `when target.os == Os.linux` folds true and a `match` without a default arm is accepted

column2: Comptime §5.1; Stdlib appendix §4.1 (STD-12: `typeinfo(T).owning`)
column3: `comptime if typeinfo(T).owning` is refused ("cannot fold this comptime condition"); read as a value, `typeinfo(Fd).owning` is accepted and answers `false` with no diagnostic; `Vec`'s `free`/`clear`/`truncate` carry no release check to guard (#1549)

column2: Functions §4.1 (an `in` aggregate is passed by reference to a copy, so the callee cannot mutate the caller's value)
column3: every legacy caller passes an `in` aggregate argument as its own place, not a copy, so a write through an `out` / `in out` parameter naming the same place shows through the `in` one; the shared IR does not build a whole store into such a parameter beside an `in` parameter that may alias it, so the program is refused at build on every backend (a located diagnostic) rather than answering the aliased value

column2: Comptime §3.2, §3.4; Functions §1.3, §1.4 (MOD-3: receiver auto-ref)
column3: x86_64: a user generic returning a type-parameter value out of a user generic struct answers a wrong value for an enum or struct argument written explicitly (`bget(E, ptr(be))`: 103 for 42), and the implicit `be.bget()` segfaults

column2: Functions §2.3 (an `in out`/`out` place argument is read and written in place); Memory §3.1/§3.3
column3: aarch64/riscv64: an array element bound to an `out`/`in out` parameter dies with SIGSEGV (139); wasm: a write to a scalar `out`/`in out` parameter traps (134), the backend having no place passing for a scalar

column2: Types §6.2 (a niche-folded `Option(ptr(T))` is one pointer word); Memory §4.2
column3: aarch64/riscv64/wasm: an enum with a folded `Option(ptr(T))` component hits the legacy fail-loud stubs, and its functions stay legacy (`ir::fn_folded_comp`)

column2: Memory §4.3 (`deref(p) = v` writes the whole pointee)
column3: aarch64/riscv64: the legacy `deref(dst) = <aggregate>` stores one word, so a whole read through `deref` stays legacy (`ir::fn_deref_whole`) and traps

column2: Modules §4.1 (an import alias names the same function as its path)
column3: aarch64/riscv64/wasm: a call through a function import alias, and in some packages a qualified call beside it, is emitted as an undefined callee and traps

column2: Modules §4.1 (an import alias is a comptime alias, erased: a call through it is the call to the aliased function)
column3: aarch64/riscv64: a call through a named function alias (`h := m::g`, then `h()`) is emitted as `brk #0 // undefined/builtin callee` and traps (133); wasm traps (134); x86_64 calls the function

column2: Modules §3, §4.1 (a use through an alias is checked exactly as a use of its spelled path would be)
column3: a use through a function alias whose path names no declaration passes check: x86_64 fails at `ld` inside the compiler, aarch64/riscv64 build and trap (133), wasm builds and traps (134); the spelled path is refused at check

column2: Modules §3 (a declaration is visible to its module, its descendants and, through `pub`, its parent; never to a sibling)
column3: check accepts a bare type name that a module neither declares nor imports, resolving it to a sibling's declaration: x86_64 answers 41 where a reject is due, aarch64/riscv64/wasm trap

column2: Functions §5.5 step (2) (within a function body its own allocator parameter is the ambient: an elided allocator resolves to it)
column3: a direct call to a non-generic function that elides its allocator parameter, inside a function with its own allocator parameter, is refused at check on every backend (a located diagnostic naming the allocator parameter, #1822) rather than bound to the enclosing parameter; a generic callee, as in the issue, is not judged and still builds and crashes (#1842)

column2: Memory §4.3; Types §6.4 (a `deref` in a value context loads the whole place; a `[T; N]` value is its `N` elements)
column3: aarch64/riscv64/wasm: a whole fixed array copied out of a pointer (`v : [T; N] = deref(p)`, `v = deref(p)`) is refused at compile time, located, instead of being copied

column2: Stdlib appendix §3.6, Types §7 (bytes(s) is the [u8] view of the str s, the same {ptr, len} pair with no copy)
column3: aarch64/riscv64: a bytes() call in a function built by the shared IR returns 133 instead of the correct value; wasm returns 134; x86_64 is correct

column2: Types §6, Memory §4.3 (a scalar field of a struct through a pointer is read from the struct's word-prefix layout)
column3: aarch64/riscv64/wasm: a word-prefix field read through a pointer to a non-word-tier struct returns the wrong value (exit 40 for 42); the shared IR builds it correctly on x86_64

column2: Grammar §2.6 (SYN-12: the continuing tokens are a closed list; a token that can begin a statement never continues a line)
column3: a line beginning with `-`, `(`, `[` or `..` is folded into the previous line: `return a` ⏎ `- 8` returns `a - 8`, `g` ⏎ `(42)` is a call, `h := g` ⏎ `(40)` crashes

column2: Types §6.4 (OP-10: an index inside a store's base keeps its guard at its own operation site, before the right-hand side)
column3: `ss[i].a[k] = v` with `i` out of range evaluates `v` before trapping

column2: Memory §6.4 (MEM-14: a captured name is read-only in the body; a receiver's auto-ref that needs a writable place is ill-formed)
column3: `s.bump()` on a captured `s` inside a closure is accepted and writes the caller's binding, even an immutable one (70 for 42)

column2: Memory §6.4 (MEM-14: a write to a captured name is refused at that use with a located Semantic diagnostic)
column3: an assignment to a captured name is refused as `unbound name`, not as a write to a capture

column2: Functions §7.1 (FN-14: a comptime-variadic's pack name is not a value; only a `comptime for` collection)
column3: every other use of the pack name passes check (`inner(args)`, `t := args`, `return args`, `args + 1`, `args.len`, a run-time `for`) and runs to a wrong value

column2: Declarations §6.1, Functions §1.4 (FN-15: a module-level function named like a prelude function joins its overload set)
column3: a program `len(u64)` hides the prelude's `len`: `len(s)` over a `str` or a slice is refused as `type mismatch` instead of calling the prelude

column2: Declarations §6.1, Functions §1.4 (FN-15: the same parameter signature as a prelude function, or a second generic definition of a prelude generic, is a redefinition error)
column3: `panic := fn(in msg : str) -> u64` and a generic `len(T : type, s : Slice(T))` are accepted

column2: Functions §5.5 (FN-16: a short call viable under both the written and the elided reading, binding differently, is ill-formed, independent of an ambient)
column3: inside `alloc::with` the ambient is spliced into such a call (195 for a refusal), and `dk(42)` silently takes the elided reading

column2: Functions §5.5 (FN-16: a short call with exactly one viable reading binds by it)
column3: inside `alloc::with`, `dk()` and `g(35)` (elided allocator plus an omitted default) are refused as `leaves parameter unbound`

column2: Declarations §6.1, Modules §4.1 (a descendant's alias `f := b::f` shadows an ancestor's `f`)
column3: the bare call in the descendant binds the ancestor's `f` (140 for 42), or fails at link when the ancestor's `f` is not emitted

column2: Modules §5; Declarations §5 (MOD-16: module scopes nest; a bare head resolves to the innermost scope that binds it, child modules included)
column3: a bare child, sibling or self module name as a `::` head is refused as `no module … in scope`; `x::f()` inside `a` resolves `x` from the package root

column2: Tooling §4.3.3 (TOOL-28: an overflowing binary-operator chain breaks after each operator)
column3: `fmt` breaks before each operator; for `-` its output begins lines that Grammar §2.6 does not continue, so the formatted program means something else once #1910 is fixed
